title: Following a Value to Its Sink
hints: A finding about a user-controlled value is a claim about its sink: the place the value leaves PHP — the markup it is printed into, the statement that is executed, the header that is sent, the path that is opened, the process that is started. Everything between the source and that point is the path, and nothing on the path decides the question. Name the sink and read the code at it, or report the finding as unverified and say which class went unread.

Following the value is one question asked at each hop: does this hop emit the value, or hand it to something else? A component that hands it on emits nothing, so its own escaping or quoting says nothing about the result, and a helper on the path that looks like an opt-out is often what keeps a value the sink already protects from being encoded or quoted twice. The last hop is usually inside an installed package rather than in the code under review, and reading it is what a security verdict costs.

Rendering: the sink of a value a template outputs is whatever writes it into the response, which is not always the template. A value handed to a page title, a meta tag or a header is emitted by that API instead, and the ViewHelper that passed it there returns nothing at all.

Database: the QueryBuilder quotes identifiers, not values. expr()->eq('field', $value) quotes the field name and puts $value into the statement exactly as it was handed over — createNamedParameter() is what makes it a bound parameter, and a LIKE value needs escapeLikeWildcards() before that or its wildcards are the caller's. The sink is the executed statement, so what decides the finding is how the value arrived there rather than which builder method was called.

Executing the path is cheaper evidence than reading it: a functional test that renders the template or runs the query and asserts what came out answers the question in one run, and leaves the answer behind for the next reader. Where a value reaches a sink and no test covers that path, the missing coverage is a finding in its own right.

title: Access Restricted Pages and extendToSubpages in the Frontend
appliesTo: subsection was found and not accessible
hints: Two questions, two methods, and only one of them walks the rootline. `RecordAccessVoter::groupAccessGranted()` reads the record's own `fe_group` and returns true where it is empty, so a page restricted only because a parent carries `extendToSubpages` passes it. `RecordAccessVoter::accessGrantedForPageInRootLine()` is the inherited form: it grants access where `extendToSubpages` is 0 and otherwise runs the full enable-field check on that page.

Which of the two a caller uses is what decides whether a restriction is inherited. `PageInformationFactory` and `PageRepository::getDescendantPageIdsRecursive()` take the rootline-aware one, so serving a page and enumerating subpages honour `extendToSubpages`. `PageLinkBuilder::shouldModifyUrlForAccessRestrictedPage()` takes the other, so a link to a page restricted only through a parent is not recognised as restricted: TYPO3 emits an ordinary link and then refuses to serve it with `Subsection was found and not accessible`, which is `PageAccessFailureReasons::ACCESS_DENIED_SUBSECTION_NOT_RESOLVED`. That is an open core report rather than a misconfiguration, so check it before spending time on the site.

`config.typolinkLinkAccessRestrictedPages = <pid>` sends a link to a restricted page to that page instead — a login page — and `typolinkLinkAccessRestrictedPages_addParams` carries `###RETURN_URL###` and `###PAGE_ID###` into its query string. `linkAccessRestrictedPages = 1` on a single typolink is the per-link override that links straight to the restricted page. Both run through the check above, so both miss a page restricted only by inheritance.

A menu's `showAccessRestrictedPages = <pid>` is the same setting one layer up: `AbstractMenuContentObject::makeMenu()` sets `disableGroupAccessCheck` for the duration of the menu and copies the value into `typolinkLinkAccessRestrictedPages` for the links it builds, so the restricted pages appear in the menu and point at the login page. `showAccessRestrictedPages.addParams` and `.ATagParams` are the two sub-keys.

The core's own functional suite already models the constellation. `typo3/sysext/frontend/Tests/Functional/SiteHandling/SlugLinkGeneratorTest.php` carries data-provider rows commented out with `@todo Fails, not expanded to sub-pages`, over a fixture in `Fixtures/SlugScenario.yaml` that has a restricted page with a subpage under it. Reproducing the inheritance case there needs no new test and no new fixture.
